categories.main_business_segments: CenterPoint Energy operates two primary business segments: Electric and Natural Gas. The Electric segment includes electric transmission, distribution, and generation operations in Texas (Houston Electric) and Indiana (Indiana Electric). The Natural Gas segment provides regulated natural gas distribution and related services across multiple states, including Texas, Minnesota, Indiana, Ohio, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Arkansas (until divestiture in 2022). The company also has a smaller Corporate and Other segment focused on energy performance contracting and sustainable infrastructure services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core operations rely on large-scale electric transmission and distribution infrastructure, including high-voltage lines, substations, and advanced metering systems (AMS/AMI). In Indiana, it owns and operates coal, gas, and solar generation assets, with ongoing investments in renewable energy (solar and wind) and grid modernization. Natural gas operations utilize extensive pipeline networks, underground storage, and advanced safety and leak detection technologies, with a focus on regulatory compliance and reliability.
categories.primary_customers_markets: CenterPoint primarily serves residential, commercial, industrial, and transportation customers. In Texas, its electric business delivers power to retail electric providers (REPs), who then serve end users. Its natural gas business serves a broad mix of residential, commercial, and industrial customers across the Midwest and South. Major end markets include urban centers like Houston, Minneapolis, Evansville, and Dayton, as well as manufacturing, agriculture, and municipal customers.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s electric operations are concentrated in the Houston/Galveston metropolitan area (Texas) and southwestern Indiana. Its natural gas distribution footprint spans Texas, Minnesota, Indiana, Ohio, Louisiana, Mississippi, and (until 2022) Arkansas and Oklahoma. The company’s service territories include major metropolitan areas and diverse regional economies in the Midwest and South.
categories.supply_chain_position: CenterPoint Energy operates primarily as a downstream utility, delivering electricity and natural gas to end users. In electric operations, it functions as a transmission and distribution utility (TDU) and, in Indiana, as a vertically integrated utility with generation assets. In natural gas, it acts as a local distribution company (LDC), purchasing gas from suppliers and delivering it to customers. The company does not own significant upstream production or midstream assets following its exit from the midstream sector.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, CenterPoint is focused on becoming a pure-play regulated utility, with increased capital investment in electric and gas infrastructure, grid modernization, and clean energy enablement. The company has announced net zero emissions goals for Scope 1 and 2 by 2035 and a 20-30% reduction in Scope 3 emissions by 2035. R&D and innovation efforts are directed toward renewable energy integration, grid resiliency, advanced metering, and supporting electrification and decarbonization initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through regulated utility rates for electric transmission, distribution, and generation services, as well as natural gas distribution. Rates are set by state and local regulators and are based on cost-of-service models, with periodic adjustments for capital investments, fuel costs, and other factors. Additional revenue streams include energy performance contracting and infrastructure services through its Energy Systems Group.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In its core service territories, CenterPoint faces limited direct competition due to exclusive or semi-exclusive utility franchises. In Texas, it is the sole TDU in its area, while in Indiana it is a vertically integrated utility. Competition exists from alternative energy sources (e.g., distributed generation, electrification, and other fuels) and, in some markets, from other gas distributors and marketers. The company is positioned as a leading regulated utility in its regions, with a focus on reliability, customer growth, and clean energy transition.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of 2021, CenterPoint Energy reported $8.4 billion in total revenues and $1.4 billion in net income available to common shareholders. The company serves over 2.8 million electric and 4.7 million natural gas customers. Recent years have seen growth driven by rate base investments, customer growth, and strategic divestitures (e.g., midstream exit, sale of Arkansas and Oklahoma gas businesses). The company has a robust capital expenditure plan exceeding $40 billion over 10 years, supporting long-term rate base and earnings growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: CenterPoint Energy emphasizes safe, reliable, and affordable energy delivery, with a strong commitment to customer service, infrastructure modernization, and sustainability. Its value proposition includes industry-leading investments in grid resiliency, advanced metering, and clean energy enablement, as well as ambitious net zero emissions goals. The company differentiates itself through its scale, regulatory expertise, and focus on innovation and stakeholder engagement in the transition to a lower-carbon future.
